summary: Miami (6-0, 48.5 PPG) is a 20.5-point favorite, but Pitt's defense is solid and its offense scores 33. Most likely to win: Pittsburgh Panthers +20.5 (-112).

extra_legs.note: Pitt scores 32.9 and allows 16.4 a game, and Miami's wins over FSU (8) and Wake (13) were close.
Miami alone averages 48.5 points, and SI listed the same total at 50.5 earlier in the week.

research:
1. Market (ESPN pickcenter/DraftKings): MIA -20.5 (-105) / PITT +20.5 (-115), total 48.5 (o-108/u-112), ML -1650/+950. SI (DraftKings) showed -20.5 (-108/-112) and 50.5 earlier, so the total has dropped 2 points.
2. QBs: Miami Darian Mensah 135/167 (80.8%), 1,764 yds, 18 TD, 1 INT (ESPN, SI). Pitt Mason Heintschel 98/148, 1,304 yds, 14 TD, 1 INT. No QB injury news found for either; backup track records not found.
3. Skill players: MIA Malachi Toney 50 rec, 758 yds, 8 TD; Javian Mallory 397 rush yds, 5 TD. PITT Damon Ferguson Jr. 438 rush yds, Cataurus Hicks 500 rec yds (ESPN leaders).
4. Team stats (ESPN): Miami 48.5 PPG, 559.5 yds, 14.0 PPG allowed, 58.5 rush yds allowed. Pitt 32.9 PPG, 450.1 yds, 16.4 allowed, 57.3 rush yds allowed, 249 pass yds allowed.
5. Miami results: 77-7 FAMU, 33-20 at Wake, 52-3 CMU, 41-13 at Clemson, 43-35 2OT vs FSU (ESPN). Margins of 70, 13, 49, 28, 8: three of five cleared 20.5.
6. Pitt results: 27-13 Syracuse, 59-0 (ESPN lists the opponent as BUCK), 35-33 at Virginia Tech, then losses 17-21 to UNC and 21-27 at BC (ESPN). Pitt is 5-2 and 2-2 in ACC.
7. Situational: No. 1 Miami hosts at Hard Rock Stadium, noon ET on ESPN; the 2001 national title team is being honored (ESPN). Big letdown or look-ahead risk is small, but a blowout lead can mean starters rest.
8. Weather: ESPN/AccuWeather 82F, 14 mph gusts, 20% precipitation. Mild wind effect only.
9. Injuries: ESPN lists no injuries for either team; I found no Miami or Pitt injury news. Treat as unconfirmed.
10. Models: ESPN matchup predictor gives Miami 92.5%. Dimers/other models were not reachable.
11. Experts: SI's Week 8 preview gave odds and Mensah's stats only; I found no named pick. No betting splits found.
12. Scheme: Miami's balanced attack (333 pass, 227 rush yds) hits a Pitt defense that stops the run (57 ypg), so Pitt may keep drives long and the clock moving. Limited scheme sources found.
13. Math: Miami (48.5 + 16.4 allowed by Pitt)/2 is about 32, and Pitt about 16-18, so the projection is 52-56 points and a 14-17 point margin vs 20.5.
14. History: not researched in depth.
15. Pricing note: the Pitt +20.5 price of -112 is SI/DraftKings; ESPN shows -115. Fair is from DraftKings' two sides.
Sources: ESPN summary/pickcenter/leaders/boxscore, SI betting preview (via search), AccuWeather via ESPN.
